title: Directed AI agents to build a real 5 km city you can walk and drive in your browser. The hard part wasn’t the code.
author: 2600th
selftext:
Most AI game demos I see are small or procedural. I wanted the opposite: a real city, street by street, at full scale.

I’m one person. AI coding agents wrote the code, and I became the director: I describe it, they build it, I look and send it back.

Four weeks later, 5 km × 5 km of a real city runs in a browser tab, built from free map and satellite data. Metro trains, traffic, crowds, rain, day to night. You can walk it or drive it.

The surprise: the agents were never the bottleneck. Seeing was.

They’d say “done”, and it was, in daylight. Then I drove at night in the rain, and every tyre mark glowed white.

So my job became noticing. Every mistake I caught became one line in a notes file the agents read before they start. That file taught them more than any prompt.

The other fix was a second agent whose only job is judging screenshots. Agents grading their own work are far too kind.

It’s not finished. People still walk through each other sometimes. But it’s real, and it’s playable.

Try it (desktop Chrome or Edge): [https://ggn-city.vercel.app](https://ggn-city.vercel.app)

If you build with agents: how do you check that what they make actually looks right?
